title: Delaying static initialization until a method is called
answer: You cannot make the static block of an already initialized class wait until an arbitrary method call; static initialization occurs on the JVM's first active use that requires initialization. However, the initialization-on-demand holder idiom moves the expensive static field into a nested class that is not initialized until that nested class is actively used. AeroTopo's `HolderRegistry` does exactly this: `Holder.INSTANCE` is initialized when `HolderRegistry.instance()` first accesses the nested Holder class.
